gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Approachable and a touch commanding, Quilon rolls its strokes from thick to slightly thinner joins while Noto Sans Samaritan stays low in contrast, with generous daylight inside its curves. Make the heading small and the display charm fades fast.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Editorial but unfussy, with no harsh thin spots anywhere. Quilon leads with lightly modulated strokes, and Noto Sans Saurashtra follows with capitals that barely rise above the lowercase, which gives the pair its quiet, level look.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sc: Quilon opens with medium-contrast strokes and tall, open a, e and s shapes that look made for a masthead. Noto Sans SC sits underneath with chalky curves that stop short of closing, so a long stretch of text feels light and unhurried.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sharada: A mild thick-thin variation, like a letterpress slug, gives Quilon its editorial authority at display sizes. Noto Sans Sharada simply does the plain work of bulky, open-formed lowercase.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Quilon has hairline-free thin strokes beside weighty stems. It carries the commanding headline voice, while Noto Sans Siddham handles the text with a large central band and an s whose ends hang wide open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Quilon's curves carry the slight thickening of a reed pen, giving headings an editorial pull. Noto Sans Sinhala runs a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, and its curve endings keep well apart, so a long page reads steadily.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo reads big and friendly, with a sizable x-height for screens and curved letters whose mouths stay wide and unclosed. Quilon is the one with presence, its medium stroke contrast built for headings, while the body simply stays legible.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Quilon brings an editorial, commanding voice, with modest stress in its curves and large open counters. Noto Sans Sundanese comes in behind with open-mouthed e crossbars and almost no gap between x-height and capitals, so the two sit together as a tidy, quiet column under a bold head.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans Sunuwar, whose curves leave daylight like a rope's open bight, and Quilon smooths the reading pace with mild thick-thin differences. Headline and text feel related but clearly separate.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri keeps short ascenders over a tall x-height, with an a whose lower bowl opens to breathe. Quilon does the commanding editorial work up top, thinning slightly where curves meet stems; the body just reads.
